items.text: A conductivity of 30 µS/cm is very low because the water contains very few dissolved ions (electrolytes).
items.why: The supplied material does not characterize 30 µS/cm as 'very low'; the operator-provided normal range is 0–1 500 µS/cm and the document lists healthy freshwater as 50–1 500 µS/cm. The characterization 'very low' is not stated as fact in any supplied source.

items.text: Very pure or de-ionized water: The ion concentration is almost zero so the solution can't conduct electricity.
items.why: The supplied material does not discuss de-ionized water or pure water as a cause of low conductivity readings. The EC_K_1.0_probe.pdf describes the operating principle but does not mention de-ionized water.

items.text: Dilution with fresh low-mineral water: Adding large volumes of water that has little dissolved salt reduces the overall ion load.
items.why: The supplied material does not mention dilution with low-mineral water as a cause of low conductivity. The water-quality document discusses EC drivers (geology runoff road salt discharges) but does not specifically describe dilution effects.

items.text: Low-mineral natural waters: Some streams or groundwater sources naturally have low total dissolved solids giving low EC.
items.why: The supplied material does not specifically state that streams or groundwater sources naturally have low TDS giving low EC. The document mentions geology and runoff as drivers but does not make this specific claim.

items.text: Sensor fouling or calibration drift: Biofilm deposits or a mis-calibrated probe can give artificially low readings.
items.why: The supplied material mentions fouling and drift generally (e.g. 'All submerged sensors foul' 'Calibration drift: pH DO and ORP probes drift over time') and the EC probe document mentions deposits causing inaccurate readings but it does not specifically state that fouling or drift produces artificially LOW readings — the EC probe document says deposits 'can change the basic electrical properties of the probe and cause inaccurate readings' without specifying direction.

items.text: In short a low EC reading means the water is very low in dissolved salts or the probe isn't measuring correctly.
items.why: This summary claim that low EC means either very low dissolved salts OR probe malfunction is not stated in the supplied material. The material does not provide this binary interpretation.
